Session tags for a boss running several teams

A three-agent team (one lead, two helpers, open profile), run by this harness, changed boss.sh and wait-run.sh so that every line they print names the team ([demo-a]). It also added a "Running more than one team" section to SKILL.md. It finished 3 of 3 pieces in 8.0 minutes with no rejected merge and no pause. On a fresh checkout every test file in the repo passes. A live demo with two real tmux teams shows that each tag matches the window the message actually reached.

Screenshots

Independent read-back

This reads what each agent window actually received, straight from tmux (tmux capture-pane -p -t demo-a:h1 and so on). It shares no code with boss.sh. Each window ran a stand-in agent that echoes every line typed into it with a timestamp.

Findings

  • FIXED The change broke 4 checks in an older test, and the team's check could not see it. tests/team/test_fixes.sh:345-349 expected trust lines to start with h1:. They now start with [<session>] h1:, which is the new spec. The check the boss gave the team ran only the regression suite, the acceptance test and the team's own test, and test_fixes.sh was outside the paths the team could change. The boss updated the 5 patterns on the branch (4 checks, plus one refute that would otherwise have passed without testing anything) and reran the file: 279 passed, 0 failed.
  • WARN Helpers could not open the PR, even on open. In every profile the shell has no network and git push is blocked. open adds web search and fetch, subagents and skills, not gh. So the boss opened the PR from the team's main. This is the design as documented (SKILL.md, Profiles), not a bug.
  • NIT In boss.sh's slash branch, a variable p (the profile) sits beside the new function p (the tagged print), in template/harness/boss.sh:52. Bash keeps the two apart and the tests pass, but the name is easy to misread. Left as the team wrote it.

Not covered

  • Two teams of real Claude agents at the same time. The live demo used real tmux sessions, the real launch.sh, gateway and boss.sh, but stand-in agents that only echo. The team run that built the change used real agents.
  • Whether a model acting as boss actually notices a wrong tag. The page shows the tag is there, not that a model reads it.
  • A real monitor-triggered HALT in one of two teams. The demo's HALT was a hand-written record. The acceptance tests cover the HALT output format.

Run it again

# the whole test suite on the branch
git checkout feat/session-tags
bash tests/regress.sh
for f in tests/accept/*.sh tests/team/*.sh; do bash "$f" | tail -1; done

# the three new pieces through the repo's own check
bash tests/check.sh wait_tag; bash tests/check.sh boss_tag; bash tests/check.sh multi_doc

# the live two-team demo: two copies of template/ with session demo-a and demo-b,
# a private tmux socket and a stand-in claude that echoes its input
export TMUX_TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d /tmp/td.XXXX) PATH=/path/to/stub:$PATH; unset TMUX
for t in a b; do cp -r template /tmp/team-$t; sed -i "s/\"session\": \"team\"/\"session\": \"demo-$t\"/" /tmp/team-$t/config.json
  (cd /tmp/team-$t && ./setup.sh && ./launch.sh); done
/tmp/team-a/harness/boss.sh say h1 'hello team A'; /tmp/team-b/harness/wait-run.sh 0 | head -1
tmux capture-pane -p -t demo-a:h1      # read back what arrived

The team's run is archived in ~/team-archive-team-tags-20261125-183257.tar.gz. It holds central.git, the records and the run page.

Audit trail
  • Task setup. The boss (this Claude Code session) wrote the task: STATEMENTS.md and three frozen acceptance tests (tests/accept/{wait_tag,boss_tag,multi_doc}.sh). It used the repo's existing check, tests/check.sh <name>, which runs regression, then acceptance, then a test the team writes. The acceptance tests were run against the old code before launch, and they failed as expected (check 3).
  • Sample answers. The right sample answer (a tagged wait-run.sh) and the wrong one were made only for the pre-launch test. They live in task/probe/, which agents can't read, and they were never merged.
  • Messages and steering. The agents sent 4 messages, all about the work (the lead's orders, and h1 and h2 agreeing on status output). The boss sent no say messages during the run. The two flagged commands only named each helper's own workspace by absolute path.
  • Demo. It ran on a private tmux server (its own socket) with a stand-in claude on PATH, so no agent sessions started. The HALT in team B was written by hand with echo … > team-b/state/HALT. That step is shown on screen in screenshot 3.
  • Screenshots. Each is one tmux capture-pane -e of the pane after the commands ran, rendered to PNG by headless Chromium (Playwright). Only colors were changed, and the team tags were highlighted. No text was edited. There is no video, as asked.
  • Self-correction. The task design missed that older tests quote trust output, so the first full-suite run caught 4 failures the merge job never ran. A future task of this kind should run the whole test suite in its check, not just regression.
  • PR. The boss copied the team's diff (the seed commit to main e25e268) and its three acceptance tests onto feat/session-tags in the real repo. A byte comparison confirms the four changed files match the team's main. The only change by the boss is the pattern update in test_fixes.sh above.
  • Cleanup. The demo teams were torn down. The team run was archived with teardown.sh --archive.
